body:
Windows x64 cannot compile the x87 assembly in `FloatingPointUnit`, and SSE has no selectable intermediate precision. Add MXCSR control access on x64, report precision as fixed by each float/double operation, and make `setPrecision` unavailable there. Restrict CollisionWorld's existing precision save/set/restore bracket to x86, keeping the declarations, implementation and caller consistent.

Rounding and exception-mask updates preserve sticky exception flags and the saved DAZ/FTZ policy. Saved control words remain architecture-specific. Win32's x87 path, including its precision setter's existing old-state behavior, remains unchanged. The Linux implementation is untouched; correcting the Win32 setter or changing the DPVS PC64 numerical reference is separate work.

One source commit: three files, +55/−2, directly above upstream `master`. The source delta and final source blobs are identical to the reviewed fork draft; the source remains independent of the CI repair. The two CollisionWorld guards exclude the integration branch's unrelated debug-logging change. Neither the LP64 history nor the SSE math package is required.

Existing native v120 [/fp:strict Debug](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/4849c510c4983fd00a0515bc309a133090ffb7ab/review/client-x64/allocator-math-next/fpu-next-debug-v3-results.json) and [Release](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/4849c510c4983fd00a0515bc309a133090ffb7ab/review/client-x64/allocator-math-next/fpu-next-v5-results.json) observations use client translation units and dependencies. This branch's FloatingPointUnit.cpp matches the recorded candidate hash exactly, and its FPU header matches the client counterpart. Per configuration, candidate and stock Win32 pass 46/46 checks, x64 passes 67/67, and the no-op x64 setter control fails 21 checks. The precision API compiles on Win32 and is rejected on x64; stock x64 assembly is separately rejected.

The fixture checks control state, sampled ±1.5 rounding, sticky flags and supported DAZ/FTZ combinations using zero-initialized production configuration defaults. It does not test configured exception startup, trap delivery or CollisionWorld execution. The server ConfigSharedFoundation source and dependencies differ from the client fixture; this is counterpart evidence, not an exact Windows server build. The packet has no independent header/CollisionWorld digest, and its stock control uses current public headers. No new Windows build or runtime run occurred during packaging; physics, Direct3D behavior and general x87/SSE numerical equivalence are not established.

[Source identity, dependencies and independent review](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/071cb6def2710b13055f330f9b311afda67ed79c/review/client-x64/pr-ready-next/server-fpu-controls/RESULTS.md).

The CI commits include the [existing workflow repair (#38)](https://github.com/SWG-Source/src/pull/38) and a manual qualification trigger. They check out the submitted head and build it in the pinned legacy container instead of invoking the broken bare-repository clone. The earlier failed upstream checks remain visible. No production file changed when adding this repair.

[Full legacy Linux32 build on this head](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/src/actions/runs/36899813580) passed at `eb75e4e007e07a7af2c9557834ebf79c3e212fa2`, including the tracked-input integrity check. This checks the Linux configuration; it does not compile or execute the Windows-only paths described above.
title: foundation: support Windows x64 floating point controls
